name: Netflix
description: Netflix sells monthly streaming subscriptions worldwide and a fast-growing ad-supported tier, and reports as one segment. It crossed 325 million paid memberships in Q4 2025. Money comes from membership fees (raised through price increases and added members) plus advertising, which was over $1.5B in 2025 and is expected to roughly double to about $3B in 2026. The big cost is content: about $17.1B of cash content spend in 2025, with amortisation guided up about 10 percent in 2026. Operating margin was 29.5 percent in FY2025 and 33.4 percent in Q2 2026, but the company guides 31.5 percent for full-year 2026. Netflix agreed to buy Warner Bros. in late 2025, then walked away in February 2026 and collected a $2.8B termination fee when Paramount Skydance won the target.

businessLines.name: Streaming memberships and advertising (single reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Customers pay a monthly subscription (price set by plan and country); the ad-supported plan adds advertiser payments per ad view. Cost is mostly content produced or licensed up front and amortised.

brands.share: All revenue; no subsidiary breakout reported
